top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a discrete invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) credited to Katori for the concept and first clock and to Ye for taking it to the 10^-18 uncertainty frontier. The result is quantitative and reproduced across species and laboratories. The two-name allocation is clean, and a citation worded around the lattice clock and its realisation stays distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. All eight members already support this slate item, so awarding it is preferable to no award.
